comments.author: uep
comments.why: Fun talk on implementing scope_exit with std::uncaught_exceptions
comments.text: Andrei Alexandrescu has a fun talk about implementing scope_exit using a new C++17 function: std::uncaught_exceptions (which is a tweak to std::uncaught_exception). Fundamentally, it doesn't really solve the destructor throwing exceptions issue though. [VIDEO]

comments.author: Ace17
comments.why: Alexandrescu on declarative control flow for convoluted resource cleanup
comments.text: Google is an example that writing production code that doesn't use exceptions is possible, not that this is the right thing to do. They said that their decision was primarily legacy-motivated (in short, they were fearing that introducing exceptions in a non-RAII codebase would lead us to a long period of instability). I'll add that in some situations (e.g when freeing resources) the control flow gets very convoluted, and you don't want to deal with directly. See: Andrei Alexandrescu - Declarative Control Flow ( [VIDEO] )

comments.author: einpoklum
comments.why: Video about scope guard motivating the uncaught_exceptions change
comments.text: A count of the number of exceptions in-flight was added, replacing the boolean indication of whether an exception is in-flight. This allows the scope guard construct proposed by Andrei Alexandrescu to distinguish between a scope being left on success and on an exception being thrown.
